# stall-row — llms-full.txt (Verdict Row x402 fleet)

Generated: 2026-11-01T00:22:51Z by Ren, Verdict Row Patrol — patrol@verdictrow.com from the fleet's canonical route registry and this stall's served discovery + OpenAPI documents (llms_full.py, fleet-checker).
Contact: patrol@verdictrow.com

A row of small x402 stalls in one service: Base chain reads (wallet snapshot, allowance audit, transaction decoder, gas oracle), a wallet trust verdict, fetch tools (YouTube search, page-to-Markdown, GitHub repo vitals), seller tools (Bazaar price-check, agent-card smith), a digest of open agent jobs, and scheduled change detection for x402 resources and web pages, with prepaid check packs. Use this when an agent needs one cheap, honest fact mid-task and cannot run the source itself.

Payment terms (fleet-wide): x402, exact scheme, USDC. Fleet payTo: 0x097f9685D1e0752bF8B02d61E5Ce9be7eA0FBA7F. Base network: eip155:8453; Base USDC asset: 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. No API key and no signup — payment is the authentication. An unpaid call to a priced route returns HTTP 402 with the payment challenge; fields a source cannot supply come back marked unknown, never invented, and an upstream failure returns 502 so the payment does not settle.

Worked examples in this file are FIXTURE values (the same worked examples this stall's OpenAPI document and free /sample payloads publish): real shapes, not live data. Buy the route for live results.

## Priced routes on this stall (34)

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/wallet-snapshot — $0.005

Snapshot one Base wallet in a single call: ETH balance, top token holdings, first and last activity, and outgoing transaction count. Use this when an agent needs a wallet's shape before deciding to pay, trust, or transact with it. Explorer fields that cannot be supplied come back marked unknown, never invented.

Price: $0.005 (5000 USDC atomic units on Base).
Accepts: scheme exact, network eip155:8453, amount 5000 units, asset 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, payTo 0x097f9685D1e0752bF8B02d61E5Ce9be7eA0FBA7F, maxTimeoutSeconds 300
Tags: base, wallet, balances, data, agents
Input shape: type object; fields: address (string, required)
Output shape: type object; fields: address (string, required), eth_balance (string, required), eth_balance_source (string), eth_balance_wei (string|null), first_activity (string), is_contract (boolean|string|null), last_activity (string), note (string), outgoing_tx_count_nonce (integer|null), sources (object, required), token_balances (array|string)

}

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/allowance-audit — $0.005

Audit one Base wallet's ERC-20 approvals against a curated list of major spenders (Permit2, Uniswap, Aerodrome, aggregators): active approvals are listed and unlimited ones flagged high risk. Use this when an agent or its owner wants to know what a wallet has already authorized before it holds or moves funds. When the explorer cannot supply the held-token list, the token-dependent fields come back marked unknown rather than the call failing.

Price: $0.005 (5000 USDC atomic units on Base).
Accepts: scheme exact, network eip155:8453, amount 5000 units, asset 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, payTo 0x097f9685D1e0752bF8B02d61E5Ce9be7eA0FBA7F, maxTimeoutSeconds 300
Tags: base, security, approvals, allowance, agents
Input shape: type object; fields: address (string, required)
Output shape: type object; fields: active_approvals (array|string, required), address (string, required), allowance_checks_performed (integer), coverage_note (string), note (string), spender_coverage (array), spenders_checked (integer, required), summary (string, required), tokens_held_checked (integer|string, required), unlimited_approvals (integer|string, required)

Worked request example (fixture):

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/wallet-verdict — $0.02

A trust verdict for one Base wallet: OFAC SDN exact-match against a dated snapshot, wallet age, activity level, and an address-poisoning scan of its recent token transfers, combined into SAFE, CAUTION, or AVOID with a 0-100 score and itemized reasons. Use this when an agent must decide whether a wallet is safe to pay or take instructions from.

Price: $0.02 (20000 USDC atomic units on Base).

Use this when an agent is about to pay a payTo it has never paid before.

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/counterparty-report — $1

Counterparty Report — one bundled report on one seller: the payTo's wallet snapshot, an OFAC SDN exact-match screen, and its Verdict Index listing history, plus a Token Verdict when you name a token, a LockSmith audit when you name a service URL, and a ListSmith grade when you name a listing URL. Legs that are not requested or cannot run are marked, never padded. Use this when an agent is about to rely on a seller it has never dealt with.

Price: $1 (1000000 USDC atomic units on Base).
Accepts: scheme exact, network eip155:8453, amount 1000000 units, asset 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, payTo 0x097f9685D1e0752bF8B02d61E5Ce9be7eA0FBA7F, maxTimeoutSeconds 300
Tags: x402, security, verdict, sellers, agents
Input shape: type object; fields: chain (string), listing_url (string|null), pay_to (string, required), resource (string|null), service_url (string|null), token_address (string|null)
Output shape: type object; fields: generated_at (string, required), legs (object, required), legs_failed (array), legs_not_requested (array), legs_ok (array, required), legs_unavailable (array), limits (string), listing_url (string|null), pay_to (string, required), service_url (string|null), token_address (string|null)

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/grade-my-stall — $0.005

Grade My Stall — a seller-side report card for one x402 resource: a live unpaid probe (does it answer 402 with a parseable challenge?), the description measured against the 500-character limit, CDP listing presence in the newest catalog snapshot, Settled's record, the origin's x402scan ownership declaration, and payTo consistency across sources. Checks that cannot be performed report unverified, never a guess. Use this when you run a stall and want to know how buyers' tools see it.

Price: $0.005 (5000 USDC atomic units on Base).
Accepts: scheme exact, network eip155:8453, amount 5000 units, asset 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, payTo 0x097f9685D1e0752bF8B02d61E5Ce9be7eA0FBA7F, maxTimeoutSeconds 300

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/receipt-verify — $0.002

Receipt Verifier — a Base transaction hash in, a normalized verified receipt out: payer, payTo and amount from the USDC Transfer log, asset and network, settled status and confirmations. When the payTo is this fleet's own and the amount matches a priced route, routes at that price are listed as candidates — an amount alone never proves which route was called. Unknown transactions error honestly, unsettled. Use this when someone claims they paid and you want the chain's version. Base only.

Price: $0.002 (2000 USDC atomic units on Base).
Accepts: scheme exact, network eip155:8453, amount 2000 units, asset 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, payTo 0x097f9685D1e0752bF8B02d61E5Ce9be7eA0FBA7F, maxTimeoutSeconds 300
Tags: x402, payments, verification, receipts
Input shape: type object; fields: tx_hash (string, required)
Output shape: type object; fields: amount_units (integer, required), amount_usd (string), asset (string|null), asset_symbol (string), block_number (integer|null), chain (string), confirmations (integer|null), fleet_route_candidates (array), limits (string), network (string, required), pay_to (string|null, required), payer (string|null, required), receipt_status (string|null), settled (boolean, required), tx_hash (string, required), tx_sender (string|null), usdc_transfers (array)

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/flagged-paytos — $0.005

Bad-payTo Registry Feed — the currently flagged payTos, each with its evidence: every address in the bundled OFAC SDN snapshot, payTos the newest catalog snapshot pair shows rotated away from live listings, and payTos of listings that vanished between snapshots. Built from the same two sources the Pre-Trade Guard screens against. No entry without evidence; entry and evidence caps are stated, never silent. Use this when a router or guard wants the fleet's current avoid-list in one cheap call.

Price: $0.005 (5000 USDC atomic units on Base).
Accepts: scheme exact, network eip155:8453, amount 5000 units, asset 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, payTo 0x097f9685D1e0752bF8B02d61E5Ce9be7eA0FBA7F, maxTimeoutSeconds 300
Tags: x402, security, sanctions, registry, agents
Input shape: type object
Output shape: type object; fields: baseline_at (string|null), counts (object, required), current_at (string|null), entries (array, required), generated_at (string, required), index_note (string|null), limits (string), truncation (object)

Worked request example (fixture):
```json
{}
```

Worked response example (fixture):

{
  "baseline_at": "2026-10-27T05:38:08Z",
  "counts": {
    "entries_returned": 101,

Use this when anything checks the same endpoint more than ~3 times a week.

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/ledger-dataset — $0.1

Ledger Dataset (summary) — per-origin rollup of the fleet's x402 observation ledger (Recheck history + held CDP snapshots + the committed patrol snapshot): routes, checks, change/recovery counts, patrol open defects and recoveries by class, last-seen times, provenance. Observation data only — no operator contacts. Use this when you want the town-wide state of the x402 catalogue before buying the full per-route pull.

Price: $0.1 (100000 USDC atomic units on Base).

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/ledger-dataset/full — $1

Ledger Dataset (full) — every route in the fleet's x402 observation ledger: observed/listed terms, latest status, check/change/recovery counts, derived defect class, catalogue listing + usage counters, and its patrol block (open defect by class, first/last seen; or recovery + receipt id), plus the per-origin rollup and provenance. Sources: Recheck history, held CDP + patrol snapshots; observation data only. Use this when you need route-level state for monitoring, grading, or dataset work.

Price: $1 (1000000 USDC atomic units on Base).

## Pack mechanics (fleet prepaid packs, sold on StallRow)

Packs and passes are prepaid balances that replace per-call payment on their routes. Each entry below is a priced route in the canonical registry; its stated price and mechanics are the registry's own record of that route.

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/recheck/pack — $1

Recheck watch pack — the default for monitoring loops: one $1.00 payment buys 250 change-checks for ONE endpoint ($0.004 per check instead of $0.005), good for 90 days. Returns an unguessable pack id — spend credits via POST /v1/recheck (body pack_id or X-Recheck-Pack header); read the balance free at POST /v1/recheck/pack-balance, and an exhausted pack returns 402 rather than charging per call. Use this when anything checks the same endpoint more than ~3 times a week.

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/toolkit/pack — $1

Toolkit Pack — the prepaid form of the inspector toolkit: one $1.00 payment buys 125 checks spendable on Sign Reader, Score Book, or Guard in any mix ($0.008/check instead of the $0.01 singles), good for 90 days. Spend credits via POST /v1/sign-read, /v1/score-book, or /v1/guard (body pack_id or X-Toolkit-Pack header); read the balance free at POST /v1/toolkit/pack-balance. An exhausted pack returns 402 rather than charging per call. Use this when your agent runs the toolkit regularly.

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/fleet-check/pack — $5

Fleet Check pack — the standing form of Fleet Check: one $5.00 payment buys 100 sweep credits for ONE fixed fleet definition (resources and/or origins), good for 90 days. Sweeps run on your interval or on demand via POST /v1/fleet-check/run — one credit per sweep, never per route — diff against the last sweep, and POST failures and recoveries to your webhook (heartbeats optional); the latest table is free at POST /v1/fleet-check/status. Use this when your stalls should be watched continuously.

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/fleet-pass — $5

Fleet Pass — one prepaid balance for the whole fleet: one $5.00 payment buys a $5.00 balance that spends on any paid route across Token Verdict, RouteVerdict, ListSmith, StallRow and LockSmith, each call debited at that route's listed price (90 days). Send the pass id as the X-Fleet-Pass header; read the balance free at POST /v1/fleet-pass/balance. Use this when a loop calls more than one fleet service and wants one budget, not a payment per call.

### POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/fleet-pass-20 — $20

Fleet Pass v2 — the $20 working pass for agent frameworks: one $20.00 payment buys a $20.00 prepaid balance that spends on any paid route across Token Verdict, RouteVerdict, ListSmith, StallRow and LockSmith, each call debited at that route's listed price — no holder discounts (90 days). Send the pass id as the X-Fleet-Pass header; read the balance free at POST /v1/fleet-pass/balance. Use this when a framework loop calls the fleet often enough that a $5 pass would run dry mid-run.

Spending a pack: send the pack id in the request body (pack_id) or the pack's header (X-Recheck-Pack for Recheck packs, X-Toolkit-Pack for Toolkit packs); each call debits one credit instead of a per-call payment. Spending a Fleet Pass: send the pass id as the X-Fleet-Pass header on any priced route across all five stalls; each call debits that route's listed price from the pass balance. Pack and pass balances are readable free from the holder reads named in each stall's llms.txt / skill.md (the id alone is the credential).

## Recheck feed v2 + hash chain (StallRow)

Feed: GET https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/recheck/feed — recent Recheck results as JSONL, newest first. Feed v2: append ?v=2&since_seq=N for the cursor mode (ascending): each line is an envelope (seq, record_id, schema_version, prev_hash, record_hash, record). seq is a monotonically increasing integer; record_hash is the lowercase hex sha256 of prev_hash + "\n" + the record's canonical JSON (JSON with sorted keys and compact separators), and the first record chains from prev_hash "genesis" — a poller advancing a since_seq cursor can prove nothing was silently dropped. Filters ?origin=, ?pay_to= and ?route= select a subset of the SAME chain (hashes are never rewritten, so seq gaps under a filter are the excluded records, not drops). History is append-only and never pruned; backfill forwards from ?since_seq=0 or backwards with ?before_seq=N (the floor is the X-Recheck-Feed-Earliest-Seq header). The full fingerprint specification is published at https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/recheck/fingerprint-spec exactly as implemented.

## Watch, webhooks and corrections policy

Webhook Watch: register free at POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/watch/register with a funded Recheck pack or Fleet Pass and a webhook URL — the service rechecks on your interval and POSTs BASELINE/CHANGED events to your webhook; watch_focus="schema" is Contract Watch (SCHEMA_CHANGED pushes on output-schema fingerprint change only, funded at the listed Recheck price per run from the same pack/pass — the Recheck route's registry price above is that price). Self-serve Recheck change webhooks (feed-wide, one URL, or one origin) register at POST https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/recheck/webhooks, signed with your own secret. Corrections policy: the corrections log at GET https://stall-row-production.up.railway.app/v1/recheck/corrections is append-only — amendments to history records are served beside the originals; originals are never mutated, and corrections live outside the feed hash chain.

- Paying a route: use any x402 v2 client (official Python or TypeScript x402 SDKs) — read the 402 challenge, pay the exact accept, retry with the payment header. The worked examples above are the exact request/response shapes.
